first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 showed that signup simplification improved SMB activation durably, and memory_86 demonstrated that shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value. Both are directly relevant to the current decline. Verifying these two will confirm whether simplified onboarding remains effective as a lever. The competitor threat and pricing pressure are real, but addressing the internal degradation in activation funnel health is the foundation for sustainable revenue—without fixing onboarding and activation, even promotional pricing will not yield durable qualified revenue. This is a standard-scale experiment focused on restoring baseline conversion health before pursuing acquisition acceleration or pricing tactics.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories: signup simplification lifted SMB activation +9% with +4% qualified revenue (memory_31), and shortened onboarding improved completion +13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention +3% (memory_86). The current 4% QoQ drop in onboarding completion and 6% drop in activation are direct signals that baseline funnel health has degraded. Reapplying simplified onboarding as a standard experiment targets the root cause of the activation decline. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by fixing the conversion foundation rather than masking symptoms with promotional pricing or referral mechanics. While the competitor's entry pricing is a threat, it is primarily targeting price-sensitive SMBs—the same segment that memory_31 showed converts better when friction is removed rather than when price is discounted. Restoring onboarding completion and activation is the durable play for sustainable revenue.
